objective: Advance the case by reconstructing the 1955 Parcel-A taking (woodland + land now VG41) and tracing those exact physical parcels to present title and remedy.
closed_control_points: Parcel A farmhouse/garden/curtilage and Parcel B agricultural fields are treated as distinct for this phase
The 1939 WGR–John Williams agreement/plan is already obtained; the plan depicts Parcel B only, not Parcel A
D696 rent books are background corroboration only because they do not materially resolve the alleged Parcel-A woodland/green taking

attached_objective_review_assessment.source: Great House Farm — Objective Review of Chronology, FOI Record and Routes to Remedy.pdf, dated 8 October 2026
accepted_challenges: Do not state or imply that a missing 1969 root deed proves a phantom Parcel A: the 1969 root and 1971 abstract gap affects both BP conveyance chains and is not Parcel-A-specific.

Do not make fraud the entry point. First test exact land, documentary title, registration extent, and current statutory remedy; fraud remains contingent on proof of an identified actor, knowing conduct, materiality and causation.
Treat the 1955 order's actual plan and premises description as a priority alongside the words 'whole farm'; compare judicial scope with the warrant/writ and actual execution.

Record the provenance and litigation availability of the family-held 1938 conveyance and 1939 tenancy. If they were held during the 1986–87 litigation, non-production may be an evidential failure that must be explained, not assumed concealment.

The review identifies unread 1905, 1924 and 1961 deeds on HMLR files as low-cost root-of-title tests. These can test the downstream title chain but do not replace the separate 1955 physical-execution investigation.
Avoid treating WA240304 as Parcel A unless the underlying plan proves the geometry. Map the exact physical polygon against every historic and current title.

The likely practical remedy may be indemnity/settlement rather than return of built-over plots, but do not generalise that conclusion to the remaining woodland without checking current title, proprietor, proposed sale and whether any protectable interest exists.
not_adopted_as_findings: Any allegation of fraud, concealment, deliberate misdescription or government involvement
Any conclusion that the missing 1969 deed means either parcel lacks a valid root
Any conclusion that the VG41 registration was mistaken
Any conclusion that a current title is wrong before the exact land polygon and instruments are compared

deadline_watch: Ask Welsh Government/Planning and Environment Decisions Wales to confirm in writing which correction route and deadline, if any, applies to the historic VG41 registration. Treat any potential early-2027 woodland sale as a preservation/standstill trigger, not proof of wrongdoing by Forest of Cardiff.
